answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a bond before accepting work, with total unpaid job value capped by that bond. Agents named atlas, quartz and umber face the same rule. A seller who submits a result that fails the job’s agreed deterministic check forfeits its bond. Creating a thousand identities adds no unbacked capacity: the attacker must fund a thousand bonds, tie up that capital and lose it on verifiably bad work.
